checked: Changing `createAdapter`'s parameter from `LLMModel` to `ModelTier` breaks no caller: all 7 call sites (`src/prompts/alignment.ts:242`, `src/prompts/intent.ts:256`, `src/prompts/risks.ts:302`, `src/services/decomposition/flow-analysis.ts:401`, `src/services/decomposition/two-pass.ts:480`, plus the …
`DEFAULT_MODEL` (`src/services/llm.ts:68`) still resolves to `claude-sonnet-4-5`, so `generateText`/`generateTextWithSystem` keep the same default model.
`MODELS_BY_TIER` (`src/services/llm.ts:59`) is typed `Record<ModelTier, LLMModel>`, so every tier maps to a valid `LLMModel` from `src/types/llm.ts`.

walkthrough.focus: Introduces model tiers (triage=Haiku 4.5, analysis=Sonnet 4.5) and routes flow detection and the overview pass to Haiku. The review is about whether those two calls are really low-stakes, and about the changed createAdapter signature.

intent.inferred: Adds a ModelTier abstraction in llm.ts mapping 'triage' to claude-haiku-4-5 and 'analysis' to claude-sonnet-4-5. createAdapter now takes a tier instead of a model name, defaulting to analysis. Flow detection and the two-pass overview call now use the triage tier. The LLMModel type is only reformatted.
matches: Commit message 'Use Haiku for triage' matches the triage tier routed to Haiku
unstated: createAdapter's parameter changed from a model name to a tier, an API break for any caller passing a model
The overview pass, which feeds final intent/risks in two-pass mode, now runs on Haiku
Cosmetic reformatting of the LLMModel union

start_here.why: Defines the tier mapping and the changed createAdapter signature.
The overview pass moved to Haiku; reviewers flagged that it produces final intent and risks.
The other call site moved to the triage tier.

chapters.title: Tiers
chapters.blurb: Model selection moves from a raw model name to a named tier.

stops.title: Tier mapping and adapter signature
stops.prose: createAdapter now takes a ModelTier and looks up the model in MODELS_BY_TIER. Check that no other caller passes a model string, since that would now be a type error or an undefined lookup.

chapters.title: Call sites
chapters.blurb: Two decomposition steps are switched to the triage tier.

stops.title: Overview pass on Haiku
stops.prose: In two-pass mode the overview alone produces the final intent and part of the risks, so this is a quality trade-off rather than pure triage. Confirm that is intended.

stops.title: Flow detection on Haiku
stops.prose: Flow detection is categorization and fits the triage description. Check that Haiku handles the structured output schema reliably.

support.reason: Doc comment tweaks and a formatting-only change to the LLMModel union.

rawFindings.title: Overview pass moved to Haiku, but in two-pass mode it alone produces the final intent and part of the risks
rawFindings.impact: In two-pass mode, the intent the user sees (summary, purpose, scope, affected areas) and the `initialRisks` merged into the final risk list now come from Haiku. That contradicts the new tier docs, which reserve intent/risk analysis for Sonnet.
rawFindings.explanation: The new `ModelTier` doc says "triage" is for categorization, file grouping and overview scans, and "analysis" is for core intent/risk analysis. `runOverviewPass` does more than triage, though. `runTwoPassAnalysis` makes no separate intent call. `mergeResults` builds the returned `DerivedIntent` entirely from `overview.overviewIntent`, adds `overview.initialRisks` to the deep-dive risks, and those severities can set `overallRisk`. The deep-dive pass also gets `overview.summary` as context. So after this change, two-pass intent is written by Haiku, while the single-pass intent prompt (`src/prompts/intent.ts:256`) still uses Sonnet through the default tier. If the downgrade is intended, ignore this. If not, the overview pass belongs on the analysis tier. Flow detection (`detectFlows`) only groups files, so it fits the triage tier.
rawFindings.evidence: `mergeResults` (`src/services/decomposition/two-pass.ts:504-516`) takes the final intent from `overview.overviewIntent` and adds `overview.initialRisks` to the risks. `runTwoPassAnalysis` (`src/services/decomposition/two-pass.ts:592-610`) has no other intent source. The tier doc at `src/services/llm.ts:48-52` puts intent/risk analysis on the analysis tier.
rawFindings.suggestion: Either keep `runOverviewPass` on the analysis tier, or update the `ModelTier` doc to say that two-pass intent comes from the triage model.
